title: CONFUSABLE_LOCAL_DECLARATION seems like an unnecessary warning
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in v4.6.2.stable.arch_linux [001aa128b], v4.7.beta3.official [860821708]

### System information

Godot v4.7.beta3 - Arch Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Fri, 22 May 2026 19:25:09 +0000 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 (nvidia; 595.71.05) - AMD Ryzen 5 2600 Six-Core Processor (12 threads) - 31.28 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

The error CONFUSABLE_LOCAL_DECLARATION doesn't make sense to me.

In the function foo() I have an inner scope which creates it's own `bar` and prints it, then the variable is freed. After that the outer scope creates an `bar` and returns it.

Because the return `bar` does not see the if scope's `bar` (like in function goo()) the error about confusable declaration does not make any sense in my opinion, but maybe I just haven't encountered a moment where this is a good error.

### Steps to reproduce

```gdscript
func _soo() -> int:
	var bar: int = 5
	if true:
		var bar: int = 3 # Expected error here. The inner scope has access to the already declared variables in the outer scopes, so the compiler does not know which one to use and throws an error.
		print(bar)
	return bar

func goo() -> int:
	if true:
		var bar: int = 3
		print(bar)
	return bar # Expected error here. The function scope does not have access to inner scopes' variables.

func foo() -> int:
	if true:
		var bar: int = 3 # Unexpected error here. The inner scope is not able to access the variables that are not yet declared in the outer scopes.
		print(bar)
	var bar: int = 5
	return bar
```
